events.text: Agents of Fzoul Chembryl delivered the scepter of the Sorcerer Kings to the dark priest, which they uncovered from ruins beneath the Gulthmere Forest. Unable to wield the artifact, but protected from its effects by his possession by Iyachtu Xvim, he hid it within the subterranean Xvimlar temple located beneath Zhentil Keep.

Faram attacked Fzoul in the temple beneath the keep, but was stabbed through the heart with the scepter of the Sorcerer Kings and killed by the priest of Xvim. In the resulting explosion the scepter shattered into five pieces, the temple was destroyed and Fzoul was imbued with arcane power. He began work on a ritual that would prevent his complete obliteration in the face of the new power within his body.

Manshoon called for a meeting with the leadership of the Zhentarim in the Citadel of the Raven, scheduled for the 9th of Ches. His sought to plan the restructuring of the organization's inner circle as well as the capture and interrogation of Fzoul Chembryl.
By 1370 DR, Amah returned to life as a small independent city-state.
In mid-Mirtul of the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR, an adventuring party sent by Andeth Ilchammar to establish diplomatic relations with Myth Nantar arrived in Agenais.
Around 1370 DR, Airspur and Cimbar reported increasing activity by sahuagin in the seas.
The Battle of Shallows occurred in 1370 DR between a huge force of orcs and frost giants and the human and dwarf defenders of Shallows, a small settlement in the Spine of the World.
By 1370 DR, the kingdom of Kirenzia appeared on the maps of the Vilhon Reach once again.
By 1370 DR, Calaunt's aggressive competition and campaign of intimidation and assassination against the neighboring town of Ylraphon helped ensure that its rival was unable to compete.
In the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR, a band of adventurers hired to defend the property of Tantran merchants in Calaunt came under attack from the mysterious "Calaunt gargoyles".
Relarn Dayspring, Morninglord of Lathander
cites: The City of Ravens Bluff, с. 27

events.text: In the year 1370 DR, the Elder Evil Pandorym began to stir from its prison in the Palace of the Purple Emperor, extending its influence across the region of Vaelan.
Slew Manshoon and purged the Zhentarim of Manshoon's Clones, gaining leadership over most of the Black Network. Summoned the Tyrantfog.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 150

events.text: Forged the Scepter of the Tyrant's Eye.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 150

events.text: In the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR, following the end of the Tethyrian Interregnum and Reclamation Wars, Amn saw large numbers of Tethyrian exiles and expatriate Amnian families arriving in Hammer of that year.
Direct trade opens between Cormyr, Myth Nantar, Naramyr and Eadraal.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 150

events.text: In the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR, during the Twelfth Serôs War, the coast of Turmish was also subject to increased attacks from koalinth and ixitxachitls.
The Shaking Plague devastated the city of Scardale Town, killing or displacing over half the population. As a result, the capital of Scardale was moved to Chandlerscross.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition, с. 135

events.text: In Firedrake Bay, the Royal Navy of the Moonshaes sank twenty ships of the reavers of Nelanther.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 23–31

events.text: Fey began to arrive in the Moonshaes, traveling through the moonwells. They settled primarily in Myrloch Vale and Winterglen Forests.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 23–31

events.text: Hammer 11-20: Manshoon discovered that his beholder allies had been working with Fzoul. Rather than confronting his former ally, he sent spies to appraise him of the activities of Fzoul and High Blade Uoumdolphin.
Hammer 21-30: Sememmon uncovered and killed the remaining agents of Fzoul within Darkhold and its surrounding holdings.
Manshoon established an alliance with the banelich and former High Inquisitor of Bane, Faram Khaldan, granted him access to a secret passageway into Zhentil Keep.
By the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR, Iljak was rebuilt and found itself in a small-scale war with the city of Hlath along the Emerald Corridor, the main trade route through Chondath.
In the month of Ches, in the Year of the Tankard (1370 DR), the Amnian settlements of Trailstone and Riatavin succeeded from Amn to join Tethyr.
Circa the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR, Sir Ardent Raphiel of Ravens Bluff was put in touch with elders of Luiren with the help of the city's Wizard Guild's Dean of Conjuration, Jerrod Korbandor.
In the month of Hammer, 1370 DR, the contingent of Tethyrian troops detected no activity from Mintar, their scouts and spies unable to even find the supposed amassed army.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 150

events.text: By the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR, Nimpeth's slavers could be encountered deep in the land of Turmish, following slave shortages and damage done by a recent war.
In 1370 DR, Ravens Bluff suffered a devastating surprise naval assault by the pirates of the of Inner Sea, costing the city most of its naval forces.
Circa the Highharvestide of the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR, Xvimlar clerics led by Ruinlord Glorganna, arrived in Reth to establish a temple of Iyachtu Xvim.

By the Year of the Tankard, 1370 DR, the high priests of Helm, Lathander, Torm and Tyr – Genas Stoutshield, Santan Argath, Athelstan Meiados, and Thallon Geiros respectively – were in agreement that it was high time Saelmur fought Mintar and liberated it from the Church of Bane.
By 1370 DR, Sembia had emerged as the strongest of the occupying forces and had planned to run out the remaining Zhents from Scardale.
The Sothillisian War was a war between the nation of Amn and the Sothillisian Empire, with the goal of recovering the lost Armory of Nedeheim, that lasted over four years, from 1370 to 1374 DR.
By as late as 1370 DR, monsters and brigands dwelt in the eastern ruins of the kingdom.
cites: Lands of Intrigue: Erlkazar and Folk of Intrigue, с. 6

events.text: In the summer of 1370 DR, the forces of Ravens Bluff rallied and confronted those of Myrkyssa Jelan, and her war ended in the six-day-long Battle of Fire River.
Later in 1370 DR, Ravens Bluff proposed the formation of a regional government in the Vast.
In 1370 DR, rumors of a new rich gold vein in Aphrunn started to surface, promising a busy future for Torl, if the rumors were indeed true.
cites: The Vilhon Reach: Dungeon Master's Reference, с. 42

events.text: The Tyrantfog was a magical ritual, empowered by Iyachtu Xvim, that Fzoul Chembryl devised to save his own life.
In 1370 DR, Ravens Bluff proposed the formation of a regional government in the Vast.
The Battle of Rocnest was the first major battle in the siege of Evereska by the phaerimm in the Year of the Unstrung Harp, 1371 DR.

In the Year of the Unstrung Harp, 1371 DR, Emperor Aetheric III abducted Eidola Boareskyr, the bride-to-be of Waterdeep's Open Lord Piergeiron Paladinson in an attempt to summon a foreign army to defeat the demons that plagued Doegan due to use of the bloodforge.

In Nightal of the Year of the Unstrung Harp, 1371 DR, dual effects of weave magic and shadow magic created an opening in the Sharn Wall beneath the Greycloak Hills, and the maligned phaerimm were released from their subterranean prison.
cites: Return of the Archwizards: The Summoning, с. 12

events.text: In the Year of the Unstrung Harp, 1371 DR, an invasion force led by Kymil Nimesin made it past the island's defenses and finally brought war to the elven retreat.

In the month of Eleasis, of the Year of the Unstrung Harp, 1371 DR, government officials in the Faerûnian city of Ravens Bluff called for mages from the city's Ministry of Art to verify the authenticity of mithril coins that were said to have come from Glantri, a non-standard form of coinage in that nation.
The Goblin War was a conflict fought in Cormyr in 1371 DR.
Azoun V was born to Crown Princess Tanalasta.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Crown Princess Tanalasta killed the ghazneth Boldovar, but also died from her wounds.
Azoun IV died, succumbing to his wounds after slaying the Devil Dragon Nalavarauthatoryl the Red.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 151

events.text: Princess Alusair Nacacia became regent.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: The Northlander kings swore fealty to the High Queen Alicia Kendrick, creating the United Moonshae Isles. This marked the first time that Ffolk and Northlanders become truly united. The Northlander kings adopted the title of "Jarl" and continued to rule their kingdoms.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 23–31

events.text: In the Year of the Unstrung Harp, 1371 DR, Senator Pristoleph took control of the city after invading it with an army that he had raised at Firesteap Citadel.
Ketheric Thorm's war was a conflict between the Chosen of Shar, Ketheric Thorm, and the Harpers that took place in the Chionthar Valley in the 14th century DR.
In the Year of the Unstrung Harp, 1371 DR, Mhartuk, the aged Overking of Lapaliiya, died of heartstop and his son, Shaliim, was crowned in his place.

In the Year of the Unstrung Harp, 1371 DR, Norheim became part of the United Moonshae Isles under High Queen Alicia Kendrick with the signing of the Treaty of Oman, which virtually ended Northlander raiding of the Ffolk.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes

events.text: In the Year of the Unstrung Harp, 1371 DR, Norland was one of the Northlander realms that agreed to put aside ancient grudges and swear fealty to High Queen Alicia Kendrick, thus joining the United Moonshae Isles.

The Return of the Archwizards, referred to in part as the Return, was the name given to a series of events surrounding the release of the phaerimm from beyond the Sharn Wall, the return of the flying city of Thultanthar to the skies over Anauroch, and the conflicts that arose between these two groups with the people of the Western and Eastern Heartlands of Faerûn.

By 1371 DR, Queen Nathglaryst's focus was on reclaiming lost relics of Telantiwar, an ancient drow kingdom, convinced that doing so could help her to finally achieve her dream of a establishing an empire.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 19

events.text: The Untheric Crusade was a conflict between the nations of Mulhorand and Unther that took place in the late years of the 14th century DR.
Around the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, the Sons of Hoar began to garner a significant following in Altumbel.

During the Silence of Lolth in 1372 DR when Lolth did not communicate with her clergy or grant them spells, a plot by the Jaezred Chaulssin (inadvertently) led to the near-complete destruction of the city on Uktar 3.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 153

events.text: In the Feast of the Moon of the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR Deep Imaskar had decided to partly break their Great Seal in order to send out scouts, spies, and explorers into the outside world, at the prompting of Lord Apprehender Ebrul Naramixna.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 153

events.text: In the following weeks the elven warriors were joined in battle by the arcanists of Thultanthar, and in Mirtul of the next year, the forces of the Lords' Alliance led by Laeral and Storm Silverhand.
In 1372 DR a Sembian wizard repeatedly attempted to call a "Dalemeet" in order to introduce a system of magical portage to transport goods along the Ashaba.
Fzoul struck an alliance between his Zhentarim forces and baatezu Gorgomorz's forces of Dragonspear Castle to bring down Daggerford. The plot was eventually stopped by a troop of adventurers.
In 1372 DR, Horgar IV used the Silence of Lolth—and the weakness it imposed on the followers of Lolth—as an excuse to attack the drow city of Menzoberranzan, thus cementing his power over his lairds.
The city of Tilverton was destroyed by the Shadovar, leaving only a crater filled with darkness, known as Tilverton Scar.
In the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, a disease known as the Wailing Death, that resisted even magical healing, killed much of the population of Neverwinter.

The Sembian cell of the Cult discovered the Well of Dragons, in the crater of a volcano, hidden behind shadow magic in Skull Gorge. This ancient graveyard, where great wyrms went to die, had a unique undead guardian, the Dire Dragon Uthagrimnoshaarl. The Cult formed the Dragonwell Cell, comprised mostly of Sembian members.

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: Fey and half-fey creatures continued to settle in the Moonshaes, with violent encounters increasing. Human settlements around Myrloch Vale were abandoned.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 23–31

events.text: In the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, the Serpent Sibyl, an avatar of Sseth during the Time of Troubles, appeared in the Scaled Halls of Varae, deep in the catacombs underneath Hlondeth.

By the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, the kingdom was led by the Lords of Imphras II, a council mostly composed of paladins or others noble champions, and Queen-regent Sambryl, the widow of King Imphras IV.
Around 1372 DR, Ransar Pristoleph cleaned out all rogue dens and monster dens in the Firesteap Mountains to protect the caravans.
In the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, not long after the peace was lifted, the Silence of Lolth began when Lolth stopped answering her priestesses' calls and granting them spells.
In 1372 DR, Teldorn and his forces were standing by, awaiting orders from Fzoul on what city to wage war against next.
By the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, the Zhents gained control of nearly all the Moonsea region.
Around 1372 DR, the citizens of Mordulkin were again clamoring for a war to annihilate hated Luthcheq.
In the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, it was said that Northlander raiders flying the colors of Iron Keep had begun to raid Ffolk settlements and merchants.
During the early days of 1372 DR, Lady Mayor Amber Lynne Thoden was revealed to be Myrkyssa Jelan in disguise by a group of adventurers.
By the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, Xvimlar planned to have the Temple of the Dark Eyes usurp the rulership of Reth, becoming one of the most influential centers of Xvim worship.
In 1372 DR, though the churches were still locked in debate, Saelmar was working to organize a mutual-defense pact against Banite attacks with the other city-states in the Land of the Lions.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition, с. 152

events.text: 646 heavy infantry
325 light cavalry
173 heavy cavalry

The Silence of Lolth (also know as the Wrath of Lolth) was a period between 28 Eleasias 1372 DR and 28 Ches 1373 DR when Lolth stopped granting divine spells, would not respond to communions of any type, and stopped all physical planar travel to the Demonweb Pits in the Abyss.
By the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, Soorenar had a reputation for aggressive rulers who preferred to purchase victories rather than fight for them.
By the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, the Shadowmasters were the absolute power in Telflamm, though few knew how powerful they really were.
By the Year of Wild Magic, 1372 DR, the Zhentarim under the command of Kara Chermosk occupied one of the upper fortresses of Tethyamar and reopened mining operations.
By Midsummer of 1372 DR, rumors spread that a powerful mercenary commander in the Vast was gathering an army of hired soldiers and adventurers.
The Treaty of Garumn's Gorge, also known as the Many-Arrows treaty, was a treaty signed to ensure peace between an upcoming orc kingdom of the Silver Marches and others of the region.
The returned lich Sammaster completed his work on the Dracorage mythal, inciting a Rage of Dragons that was independent of the King-Killer Star appearing over the skies of Toril.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 153

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: Cult-summoned abishai burned down the Nightwind Academy in Lyrabar.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 153

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: The army of Impiltur, allied with the spirit dragon Vorasaegha, managed to destroy the Cult lair located in the Gray Forest.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 153

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: The black wyrm Zarlandris from Glaun Bog destroyed the Tower of the Rising Moon in Daggerdale before being slain. Lord Theremen Ulath swore to rebuild the dale's seat of power.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 154

events.text: While impersonating the reborn Witch-king Zhengyi, Sammaster raised an army of orcs and giants in the realm of Vaasa. After assaulting the Bloodstone Gates, the monstrous horde poured into the nation of Damara.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 154

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: King Gareth Dragonsbane responded to the threat with the Damaran army, but fell in battle after Cult members who had infiltrated his ranks betrayed the paladin-king.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 154

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: Sammaster and his phylacteries were finally, permanently destroyed. The Rage that had affected dragons for most of the year finally came to an end.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 154

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: In the Year of Rogue Dragons, 1373 DR, As'arem suffered from dragon attacks owing to the Rage of Dragons that year, and joined their allies to face a flight of dragons at Myth Nantar.
At the end of the Silence of Lolth in 1373 DR, the Jaezred Chaulssin moved to control the ruins of Ched Nasad.
Along with other realms across Faerûn, Impiltur was devastated by the Rage of Dragons that had been instigated by the evil mage Sammaster and the Cult of the Dragon.
Unknown: Sammaster resurrected Algashon as a banelich, with the intention to restore his rank as Second Speaker within the Cult.

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: Elesias 7: The red dragon Thraxata set fire to much of the countryside of Battledale.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition, с. 154

events.text: Hoondarrh, an ancient red dragon, attacked Caer Callidyrr. Massive fires burned a significant part of the city. Hoondarrh was turned away only after the Great Druid Robyn Kendrick returned from the Feywild, heading to the city with a cohort of powerful druids. High King Keane was killed while defending the city.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 23–31

events.text: In 1373 DR, in the midst of Sammaster's Rage of Dragons, the red great wyrm Balagos flew over the Land of the Lions and unleashed a firestorm in Mintar and Saelmur, killing over half of the population of both city-states.

The Siege of Menzoberranzan was a siege of the drow city of Menzoberranzan by the combined forces of Horgar Steelshadow of Gracklstugh and Kaanyr Vhok's Scoured Legion with the secret backing of the Jaezred Chaulssin over 1372 to 1373 DR.
During the Dracorage of the Year of Rogue Dragons, 1373, on Hammer 23rd a flight of dragons destroyed Ylraphon.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 153

events.text: The War of The Spider Queen was a series of conflicts that took place in the drow cities of Menzoberranzan, Ched Nasad, Eryndlyn, and Maerimydra and others in the Underdark over 1372 and 1373 DR during the Silence of Lolth.

The Elven Lord Seiveril Miritar of Evereska, leading his crusading army en route to Shadowdale stopped at Lake Sember. There he revived the Dales Compact with Battledale, Deepingdale, Mistledale and Shadowdale.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 155

events.text: House Dlardrageth destroyed the Standing Stone after defeating the army of Hillsfar, which had previously held an alliance with the drow just a month before. The army of drow were routed in battle by the Crusade a few weeks later in Myth Drannor, albeit at the cost of Lord Miritar's life.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 156
The Grand History of the Realms, с. 155

events.text: The Cormanthor War officially began.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 156

events.text: Sharran assassins infiltrated Elminster's tower in Shadowdale. An intense battled ensued, resulting with the tower being shifted to another plane of existence and its namesake wizard disappearing altogether.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 158

events.text: The Army of Darkhope, under command of Scyllua Darkhope, invaded Shadowdale with little resistance.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 158

events.text: Upon entering Shadowdale with a contingent of elven allies, Storm Silverhand and Dove Falconhand were critically injured by interactions between their silver fire and the weave.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 158

events.text: In exchange for securing powerful weapons for this battle from a shalarin priestess of Umberlee, Tu'ala'keth, the eadar was forced to swear that all of As'arem would pay homage at Umberlee's temples once each tenday through the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR.
The Battle of Daelyth's Dagger took place on Tarsakh 11, 1374 DR, between the daemonfey and their minions, and the Argent Legion and the elves.

The Battle of the Cwm took place in the early hours of Ches 27, the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, between the daemonfey army and an elven coalition from Evereska and Evermeet, on the West Cwm on the outskirts of Evereska.
In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, several armed conflicts among neighboring nations sparked among the Blade Kingdoms, the Border Kingdoms, Chessenta, and Threskel.

The Cormanthor War was a very complex war fought in Cormanthor and the Dalelands in the late 14th century DR that saw Shadowdale occupied by Zhentil Keep and then liberated, the rout of the daemonfey, and ended with the restoration of an elven kingdom in Myth Drannor.

By early 1374 DR, Deep Imaskar was besieged by the forces Pandorym had amassed, and its continued existence was in jeopardy; an Imaskari vengeance taker, Iahn Qoyllor, was dispatched to fetch Ususi Manaallin.
In Tarsakh 17 of Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, the seal on Pandorym was restored by Ususi, Iahn, and other adventurers, though much ruin was left in Deep Imaskar.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 155

events.text: In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR the Island Kingdom was assaulted by Daemonfey.
Allied with House Jaelre and Auzkovyn Clan to prevent The Return in Myth Drannor.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 156

events.text: Ordered Scyllua Darkhope to seize Moonsea Ride.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 156

events.text: Ordered Scyllua Darkhope to invade Shadowdale with the aid of the Church of Shar and the drow of House Dhuurniv.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 157

events.text: In 1374 DR Lady Sarya Dlardrageth, the half-fiend gold elves of House Dlardrageth and their Fey'ri forces arrived in Myth Drannor after a failed attack on Evereska.
The clergies of Cyric and Shar in Cormyr conspired to tear a hole in the Weave to create a vast Dead-magic zone.
cites: Cormyr: The Tearing of the Weave, с. 4

events.text: Kaedthis, the leader of one of the cults of the moon, sought to recapture the city and take control of its mythal.

The army of Seiveril Miritar, leading a return to Faerûn, recaptured Myth Drannor and its new Coronal, Ilsevele Miritar, began restoring the city to its former glory. As of 1479 DR, the city occupied a smaller area than it once did, and some parts of the ruins of the older city were still present, the forest having regrown to cover them. Myth Drannor's mythal was repaired and was active in 1479 DR, preventing access to the city from other planes.
In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, Lord Nasher was targeted in an assassination attempt by agents of the King of Shadows.
By 1374 DR, the only remnants of the long-razed Aelinthaldaar were crypts beneath the Pantheon Temple of the Seldarine, and the magic that prevented the plateau from collapsing.

After the destruction of the lich Sammaster, the Cult underwent a period of upheaval. Several cells tried to seize power in the absence of strong leadership, while the church of Tiamat attempted to absorb the Cult as a whole under the reign of the Dragon Queen. The Great Bone Wyrm, Alasklerbanbastos, tried to unite the Cult cells that continued to operate during this time, but his allegiance to Tiamat's clergy was a compromising factor.

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: In the wake of the Great Bone Wyrm's bid for leadership, an uneasy alliance formed between existing Cult leaders. Comprised of the Shadow dragon Aurgloroasa, the dracolich Daurgothoth and the humanoid lich known only as the First Interpreter, a ruling council formed within the Cult known as The Triumvirate claimed leadership. The First Interpreter was actually the risen Algashon, who kept his former identity hidden from his contemporaries.

src.title: History of the Cult of the Dragon

events.text: Klythorn 16: Mercenaries from Sembia, who had allied with House Dlargrageth, crossed Blackfeather Bridge and began an occupation of Battledale.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 155

events.text: In the Grampalt Highlands, firbolg were once again enslaved by the fomorians. The enslaved firbolgs are used to attack the inhabitants of Oman's Isle. By the middle of summer, the entire island was controlled by the fomorians.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 23–31

events.text: In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, a small group of drow arachnomancers took over one of the ancient Illefarn ruins, interestingly enough, located in the deep jungles of Samarach of the Chultan Peninsula.

In 1374 DR, Ivar Devorast, the chief builder of the canal, then detonated a large number of smokepowder charges along the length of the canal in key points that caused it be destroyed, because he felt the quality of his original vision had been lost.
In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, the Miyeritari city of Rhymanthiin was ressurected with the help of Khelben Arunsun.

Early in the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, Yenael sent her daughter Ythnel to Luthcheq as an unwitting agent, and ultimately, she and survivors of the defeated Mage Society rebels escaped to Mordulkin.
In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, tlincallis emerged from sinkholes to attack Murann and settlements in Amn, and demanded repayment for treasures plundered from Maztica.
In 1374 DR, Rivalen and his brother Brennus orchestrated a plot that brought Sembia under control of the empire as a vassal state.
In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR a group of fomorians from the Feywild, under the command of the evil Queen Connomae of Vor Thomil, invaded Oman through a gate in the Grampalt Highlands.
By 1374 DR, Helbareim still reigned amongst this swirl of influence.
In 1374 DR, Nightal 15, under the cover of darkness, an army of Zhentarim, lead by Scyllua Darkhope, invaded Shadowdale with assistance from the Church of Shar and the drow House Dhuurniv.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 158

events.text: In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, the fomorians and cyclopes of Vor Thomil invaded Oman's Isle via a portal in the Grampalt Highlands.
In the Year of Lightning Storms, 1374 DR, Westgate faced unrest caused by a guild war between the infamous Night Masks and a new organization knows as the Ebon Claws.

Lord Mourngrym was freed by a group of adventurers, inspiring the citizens of Shadowdale to join in deposing the occupying Zhentarim and killing their commander, Scyllua Darkhope. Mourngym retired as leader of the dale to rejoin the Knights of Myth Drannor; the citizenry bestowed the Pendant of Ashaba to Azalar Falconhand who claimed the throne of Shadowdale.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 158

events.text: Blamed all of the Black Networks' failures in the Cormanthor War on Scyllua Darkhope to save face with his drow allies.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 158

events.text: The ancient city of Karador surfaced in Myrloch. The return of Sarifal was declared by the fey queen Ordalf, who declared herself ruler of the entirety of Gwynneth.
cites: Dragon 362: Grand History of the Realms: The Moonshaes, с. 23–31

events.text: The planar barrier separating the Feywild from the Prime Material plane began to weaken in the Moonshaes, permitting otherworldly creatures to pass into Myrloch Vale and the forest of Winterglen.

In the following year, while agents of Shar obliterated the city of Ordulin with a catastrophic spell learned from the tome The Leaves of One Night, Lord Shadow Telamont Tanthul and his right hand Hadrhune sought out one of the sets of Nether Scrolls which had been stolen from the ancient Netheril Empire and transformed into the Golden Grove of the Windsong Tower, by the elven high mage Tyvollus Aluviirsan.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms

events.text: By Tarsakh 3 of Year of Risen Elfkin, 1375 DR, Phlan had been fully conquered by the forces of Zhentil Keep.
In the Year of Risen Elfkin, 1375 DR, High Lady Ordalf moved the city of Karador through a portal from the Feywild and it rose from the depths of Lake Myrloch.
In 1375 DR, a rift had been growing within Council of Zulkirs and opposing factions were forming under the leadership of Aznar Thrul and the necromantic lich Szass Tam.

The War of the Zulkirs was a civil war in Thay that took place from 1375 DR to 1385 DR, between the self-proclaimed regent of Thay, the lich Szass Tam, and the combined forces of the other zulkirs: Lallara Mediocros, Nevron, Yaphyll, Lauzoril, Kumed Hahpret, Mythrellan, and Samas Kul under the guidance of Dmitra Flass.
In the end however, Mordoc too was defeated and the city saved in the Year of the Bent Blade, 1376 DR.

With his drow allies broken, Fzoul offered peace terms to the elves of Cormanthor, who accept. Ilsevele Miritar gave Hillsfar and the lands directly to the north to the Zhentarim, as well as free passage along the Moonsea Ride and Rauthauvyr's Road so long as they do not fell a single living tree, injure or kill any elf, or leave the road for more than 30 paces.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 158

events.text: By 1376 DR, after the death of the drow god Vhaeraun, the dark elves were shaken and easily routed from Elven Court by Ilsevele and her army.
In the autumn of 1376 DR Luskan was attacked by an army of mercenaries led by Lord Brambleberry of Waterdeep and aided by the famous Captain Deudermont.
In 1377 DR, the Srinshee returned and granted the Rulers' Blade to Ilsevele, who drew it successfully and became the first Coronal of the Present Age.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 155–158

events.text: In 1377 DR, the Srinshee returned to the City of Song and granted Ilsevele the Rulers' Blade.
By 1377 DR, the city was reportedly home to hordes of undead while a small number of Maerimydran survivors had been aided by the Church of Eilistraee to rise to the surface.
Four Day War between Cormyr and the Empire of Netheril.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: In the Year of the Lost Keep, 1379 DR, Q'arlynd Melarn was accepted into the Conclave of the School of Ancient Arcana.
By the Year of the Blazing Hand, 1380 DR, the Netherese controlled all of Sembia, and within 20 years had fully consolidated it into their empire.
In 1383 DR the returned empire of Netheril embarked on a campaign of conquest against the Moonsea with the commencement of the Shadowbane War.

During the Shadowbane War of 1383 DR however, Cvaal forged an alliance with the dark fey of the Quivering Forest, and managed to slay a Shadovar prince, thereby ensuring that his city did not meet the same fate as Zhentil Keep.
cites: Dungeon 170: Monument of the Ancients, с. 65

events.text: The Shadowbane War was a conflict waged between Netheril and the Zhentarim in the Year of the Vindicated Warrior, 1383 DR.

In the Year of Three Streams Blooded, 1384 DR, divine conflict saw Helm, God of Guardians, slain by Tyr, God of Justice, leaving the Hellriders, the High Rider, and Elturel itself without their favored god.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: Azoun V was crowned king at 13 years old, ending the Steel Regency. Alusair Obarskyr was named High Marshal of Cormyr.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Lack of support from the nobles prevented the young king from passing his first Royal Decree that sought to give “freemen” a hearing before other “freemen” when they were accused of a crime, even if a noble made the accusation.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 159

events.text: In the following decade, Faerûn suffered the Spellplague, a cataclysmic event that reshaped both civilizations and the land itself.
The Blood War was an ancient conflict that raged between the fiends of the Lower planes.
In the Year of Blue Fire, 1385 DR, when the Spellplague struck and ravaged across Faerûn, contact was lost with Evermeet.
The Spellplague resulted in the loss of roughly one third of the War Wizards.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Tilverton Scar became the only known plagueland in Cormyr.
Native Dambrathans rebel against the Crinti kingdom and reclaim the nation from their rule.
Imbrar II dies, leaving no heir. Power devolves to the lords of the individual cities, who soon come together to form the Grand Council.
In the Year of Blue Fire, 1385 DR, three great tragedies devastated the kingdom of Impiltur.
In the Year of Blue Flame, 1385 DR, the Spellplague struck Toril and a cataclysm destroyed Halruaa.
In 1385 DR the Spellplague struck Olleth and a third of the morkoth mages dissolved in blue flashes.
In the first decade following the Spellplague of 1385 DR, the waters of the Sea of Fallen Stars receded, leaving many port cities high-and-dry, including the likes of Ravens Bluff.
In 1385 DR, Samarach and much of the Chultan Peninsula were devastated by the Spellplague and pulled beneath the sea.
In the years immediately after the Spellplague of 1385 DR, trade across Faerûn ground to a halt and Scornubel's fortunes plummeted.
The Second Era of Skyfire was a period of hostilities between the efreeti Memnon and the djinni Calim in the late 14th and 15th centuries DR.
In the Year of Blue Fire, 1385 DR, only twenty-one years after the the Baron and his Band of Iron took control, a great calamity overran Toril.
In the wake of the Spellplague of 1385 DR, a part of Shyr was exchanged with its equivalent regions in Faerûn: eastern Chondath and western Chessenta.

The Spellplague, called the Blue Breath of Change by the inhabitants of Abeir, was a disaster that struck Realmspace and even the planes themselves on the date of Tarsakh 29 in the Year of Blue Fire, 1385 DR, and was caused by Mystra's assassination at the hands of Cyric and Shar.
By 1385 DR the warring factions of Thay arrived at a stalemate.
In the Year of Blue Fire, 1385 DR, during the Spellplague, the Abeiran nation of Tymanchebar was dropped onto the region of Unther, whose kingdom in turn was transported to Abeir.
In 1385 DR, most of Unther was engulfed by the Spellplague and transported to the world of Abeir.
Mystra was assassinated by Cyric, an act that destroyed the Weave and triggered the Spellplague.
The temple of Mystra in Harrowdale was destroyed when all the temple wards go haywire simultaneously, killing head priestess Llewan Aspenhold and most of her clergy.
The Fall of Stars in Harrowdale is shrouded in a halo of blue flames for a full day, but otherwise seems untouched.
At the same time, the worlds of Toril and Abeir were undergoing their periodic planar conjunction. This proved to be apocalyptic, because it allowed the Spellplague to unravel both worlds.

Dweomerheart was destroyed, killing Savras in the process. Azuth and Velsharoon were sent across the planes and disappeared without a trace. While Velsharoon actually died, Azuth was only presumed dead. Asmodeus fused with the dying Azuth, saving the God of Wizards' life but stealing his divine powers, and thus the archdevil underwent his apotheosis.
Halruaa, Sespech, the Golden Plains, and the Nagalands were destroyed by the blue fire storm caused by the destruction of the Weave, and were reshaped into the Plaguewrought Lands.
The Spellplague infected portals and planar magic, shaking the planes and spreading to the world of Abeir.

In Abeir, the fortress of Glaur exploded on contact with the Spellplague, in a blast of power akin to the Tearfall, sending the continent of Laerakond to Toril. The cataclysm created the Glaur Barrens in Gontal.
cites: Dragon 375: Gontal: Dominions of Nehu, с. 78
Heroes of the Elemental Chaos, с. 33

events.text: Djerad Thymar was separated from Skelkor and fell on Unther, creating the Black Ash Plain and sending Unther to the continent of Shyr in Abeir.
Laerakond was sent to the Trackless Sea, were it subsumed the lands of Maztica. Maztica was transported to Abeir, and Laerakond, which became known as 'Returned Abeir', remained on Toril.
Taking advantage of the planar instability, the new god Asmodeus sent the Abyss to the Elemental Chaos in a failed attempt to end the Blood War.
cites: Fire in the Blood: Hardcover 2014, с. 94

events.text: Cormyr was struck hard by the Spellplague, but not so violently as other nations. Roughly one third of all the War Wizards were slain, driven mad, or simply disappeared in the year following Mystra's death.

Kepeshkmolik Thymara, guided by the goddess Selûne, reconstructed Djerad Thymar above the God-Tomb of the death Untherite god Nanna-Sin. The dragonborn spent the rest of the year fighting the spellscarred horrors of the former lands of Unther while founding the nation of Tymanther.
cites: Ashes of the Tyrant: Hardcover, с. 291–294

events.text: During the Spellplague in the Year of the Halfling's Lament, 1386 DR, the entirety of Luiren was believed to be submerged in the Great Sea and was called the Gulf of Luiren.
A portion of Shyr violently changed places with large sections of Chondath and western Chessenta. Displaced genasi quickly set about creating a kingdom of their own, Akanûl.
Large portions of the Sea of Fallen Stars collapsed into the Underdark. When the sea level reached its new equilibrium, the average drop in water level measured nearly 50 feet.
The waters of the Vilhon Reach were similarly drained, uncovering several ruins from ancient Jhaamdath.
The Arnrock volcano in the Lake of Steam erupts violently, wiping out the halfling settlement that had sprung up on its long dormant crater.

The Emerald Enclave sent agents throughout the Vilhon Wilds to try to counter the effects of the Spellplague. As time passed, their original mission changed from one of respect for and guardianship of nature to a vain struggle against forces far beyond their control.
Bullywug tribes from the Farsea Marshes began to thwart Zhentarim forces operating throughout the Tunlands, diminishing Black Network activities in the region.
Some of the remaining War Wizards began cross-training with the Purple Dragons in swordplay and martial defense, eventually becoming swordmages.
Fiirnel'ther Vandree of House Vandree of Menzoberranzan assassinated her mother, Troken'ther, and took the leadership of her House.
The Gundwynd Clan was rendered extinct in Waterdeep after the Spellplague first struck the city. All members were permanently transformed into trolls or giants.
A strange black monolith appeared along Cormyr's coast, never in the same place twice.
The death of Dowager Dragon Queen Filfaeril. In her last known living appearance, Alusair attended the funeral, where she privately argued with her nephew King Azoun V before disappearing from court.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Filfaeril Obarskyr died. Alusair Obarskyr disappeared shortly after her burial.
Arilyn Moonblade began training Azariah Craulnober at the behest of the latter's father, Elaith Craulnober.
cites: Realms of Infamy: The More Things Change

events.text: The human druid Zalaznar Crinios, transformed into a treant for his service to nature, took hold of the druid circle in Cedarspoke. A lesser druid called Firemane, rose to prominence in the same circle.
The elves of the militant Eldreth Veluuthra seized control of the Hullack Forest to use it as a base for their anti-human operations.
The Eye of Justice drove out Orbakh and the Night Masks from Westgate.
Auril's Winter Hall assimilated the Winged Mother's floating palace into her domain.
Randal Morn, the legendary leader of Daggerdale died. Sathrin Cormaeril arrived to Daggerdale not long after, and claimed the throne.
The town of Pros became a vassal-state of Cormyr, soon followed by its sister town of Ilipur. However, the two trading towns were ultimately ruined by the receding of the Sea of Fallen Stars.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: The city of Pros became a vassal-state of Cormyr in order to protect it from the ravages of the Spellplague. By year's end, Ilipur joined Cormyr as well.
The receding waters of the Sea of Fallen Stars ruined small trading towns along its shore.
In the Year of the Ring, 1393 DR, they formed the neighborhood of Tidetown in the new construction built near the lower level of the Inner Sea.
In 1393 DR several kuo-toa left Olleth and founded the colony of Taunissik
Sembian investors began to buy lands in the southern Dales. Concerned, Azoun V issued a formal objection to the Dale's Council in Archendale, but the King's emissary was rebuffed.
Spellscarred beings and pilgrims hoping to obtain a spellscar began to journey to Plaguewrought Lands.
A brief conflict with the Eldreth Veluuthra, a militant group of human-hating elves that controlled Hullack Forest.
The Grand Cabal of the Emerald Enclave began to stem the tide of spellscarred pilgrims that journeyed through Turmish.
The city of Daerlun became a vassal-state of Cormyr.
The war between Cormyr and Sembia began.
In the spring of Year of Silent Death, 1395 DR, a black monolith appeared not far from Reth's coast following a violent thunderstorm.
The Empire of Netheril came across the Lost Vale and displaced the saurials there into the Underdark.
Sakkors, a Netherese enclave, reappeared over Daerlun. Civil unrest broke out throughout the city, and Azoun V sends elite swordmages to restore order.
A great plague known as the Putrescent Anathema devastated the Goldenfields and Waterdeep, primarily to the poor as the supply of grain plummeted.
Most of the effects of the Spellplague had come to an end by this year and most arcane magic had returned to a semblance of normality, with a handful of major changes to the way spells were cast.
Azoun V married Nalara Marliir.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Daerlun was annexed into Cormyr.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18

events.text: Laspeera Inthré becomes Court Wizard after the death of Caladnei and began tutoring Ganrahast for the role of Royal Magician.
cites: Dungeon 198: Cormyr Royale: The Royal Court of the Forest Kingdom, с. 17–18
